source.title: Quantum metrology of rotations with mixed spin states

definition.k: Complex dimension of the subspace, not number of displayed states with individual AC properties.
definition.t: Every normalized vector in the whole subspace is at least t-anticoherent.
definition.compressionCondition: B^† T_{LM} B=0 for all 1≤L≤t and −L≤M≤L.
definition.reducedCrossCondition: Tr_{N−t}(|ψ_a><ψ_b|)=δ_ab I_{Sym^t}/(t+1) for an orthonormal basis.
definition.generalBasisCondition: For a nonorthonormal full-rank basis, Tr_{N−t}(|v_a><v_b|)=<v_b|v_a> I/(t+1).
definition.warning: Checking only the diagonal reduced states is insufficient; all coherent superpositions require the cross conditions.

bounds.proof: Choose a common symmetric t-qubit basis in the maximally entangled Schmidt decomposition of every orthonormal code vector. The cross-reduction condition makes all k(t+1) partner vectors mutually orthogonal in Sym^(N−t)(C²), which has dimension N−t+1.

Let s=floor(t/2), and choose Hilbert–Schmidt orthonormal spin tensor operators A_α spanning ranks 0,...,s. There are (s+1)² such operators. Every A_α†A_β is a linear combination of tensor ranks ≤2s≤t, so its compression to V is Tr(A_α†A_β) I_V/(N+1)=δ_αβ I_V/(N+1). Therefore the k(s+1)² vectors sqrt(N+1) A_α|ψ_a> are orthonormal in H^(j), of dimension N+1.
bounds.attribution: An independent consequence of the paper’s compression characterization and standard spin-tensor product decomposition; no novelty claim.
bounds.consequence: For t=2, k≤floor((N+1)/4). With E2 this proves the maximum dimension is exactly2 at N10,t2; the paper bound alone is3.

figure2.status: numerically found dimensions, not rigorous maxima
figure2.notes: Read from the complete figure. A reported zero is not a nonexistence proof; use independent bounds/exclusions when available.

families.centerCondition: Append |D_N^(N/2)> only for integer j with 2j−3−4floor((j−1)/2)>0, equivalently positive even integer j.
families.verifiedDimension: floor((j−1)/2)+1+1_{j positive even integer}. For integer j≥1, this equals floor(j/2)+1.
families.proof: Different supports are separated by at least two; every basis vector balances opposite m, so Jz compression vanishes and all J± compression entries vanish.

families.weights: Let u=j−3a, v=j−3a−κ−1, μ=j(j+1)/3. α²=(μ−v²)/(2(u²−v²)), β²=(u²−μ)/(2(u²−v²)); amplitudes α,β,β,α.
families.admissibility: Use only nonnegative integer a with all four indices in [0,N], positive weights, and global support separations at least3. Direct verification determines the emitted dimension.
families.proof: All supports are at least three apart, eliminating every rank≤2 ladder term, including cross terms. Opposite m pairs eliminate the first diagonal moment, and α,β solve the second diagonal moment exactly.

sourceCaveats.issue: The integer-j dimension in printed Eq48 omits the explicit condition for adding the middle vector in the preceding text. At j3, the pair with m=±1 has nonzero J+ cross matrix element with m0.
sourceCaveats.handling: Retain the Eq47 support condition and verify all matrix elements.

sourceCaveats.issue: The printed minimum contains a floor on its first argument only. At j10, κ4 gives literal k2=5/3.
sourceCaveats.handling: Do not assign a fractional dimension or claim an intended correction; count admissible integer basis vectors and verify the subspace condition directly.

sourceCaveats.issue: Eq13 prints the sum m1≤m2, while the Hilbert–Schmidt trace in Eq14 sums all ordered matrix entries. Their numerical values are not generally equal. The simultaneous zero condition after summing all M remains the relevant characterization.
sourceCaveats.handling: Use the complete matrix compression Frobenius norm, including both off-diagonal directions.

sourceCaveats.issue: Basis coefficients are approximate and the listed vectors are not normalized. Lemma1 permits a nonorthonormal basis, but projector/purity calculations need normalization or orthonormalization.
sourceCaveats.handling: Keep the raw decimals with provenance and verify the normalized entire span numerically.

exactWitnesses.basisConvention: Normalized Dicke basis, r=0,...,N; the paper spin basis is ordered m=j,...,-j, so r=j-m.

reference.construction: Independent sparse-moment construction; uses the paper definition and Eq. 8 tensor structure.

exactWitnesses.proof: All occupied Dicke indices are at least four apart, eliminating every off-diagonal tensor component through rank3. Reflection-symmetric probabilities cancel Jz and Jz³. The chosen p,q enforce 2p*j²+2q*(j−a)²=j(j+1)/3, so every diagonal rank1–3 multipole vanishes.
